title: The Dark Side of the Moon
note: A prism, a spectrum, and one of music’s most recognizable visual identities.

title: Abbey Road
note: A crosswalk turned into a cultural landmark. Four figures, one perfectly ordinary street.

title: Rumours
note: The theatrical pairing of Stevie Nicks and Mick Fleetwood, photographed by Herbert Worthington.

title: Unknown Pleasures
note: Peter Saville’s pulsar waves give scientific data an unexpectedly emotional presence.

title: OK Computer
note: Stanley Donwood and Thom Yorke’s fractured landscape of technology and unease.

title: Nevermind
note: An underwater photograph that became the defining image of a generation of guitar music.

title: Aladdin Sane
note: Brian Duffy’s portrait turns a lightning bolt into a lasting symbol of reinvention.

title: Purple Rain
note: Purple light, a motorcycle, and a world built around Prince’s unmistakable presence.

title: Thriller
note: A white suit and a relaxed portrait by Dick Zimmerman: spare, confident, instantly familiar.

title: Hounds of Love
note: A dreamlike portrait with two hounds, photographed by John Carder Bush.

title: Blue
note: A close-cropped blue portrait that feels as intimate as the songs inside.

title: Kind of Blue
note: A performance portrait by Jay Maisel captures the quiet intensity of Miles Davis.

title: A Love Supreme
note: Chuck Stewart’s contemplative portrait gives this spiritual landmark a human center.

title: What’s Going On
note: Rain, a raised collar, and a gaze that looks beyond the frame.

title: Songs in the Key of Life
note: A warm, concentric portal into Stevie Wonder’s expansive musical world.

title: Discovery
note: A liquid-metal wordmark with a rainbow edge, as playful and futuristic as the record.

title: Selected Ambient Works 85-92
note: A stark emblem suspended in negative space. Electronic music reduced to a symbol.

title: Illmatic
note: A childhood portrait layered over Queensbridge connects memory, place, and storytelling.

title: The Low End Theory
note: Red and green contours turn a painted figure into an unmistakable graphic rhythm.

title: To Pimp a Butterfly
note: A dense black-and-white group portrait that invites a closer reading of every face.
